previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with congenital tracheobronchomalacia and tracheostomy status was admitted for dyspnea, cough, green tracheostomy secretions, odynophagia, and neck pain lasting one week. She had recent hospitalizations for similar symptoms without confirmed infection. Evaluation showed no fever, normal white blood cell count, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Empiric antibiotics were given in the ED but discontinued due to lack of infection markers. Symptoms were attributed to airway irritation from inconsistent humidification. Pain was managed with opioids, and tracheostomy care was reinforced. She remained stable, symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with updated medications, a limited supply of oxycodone and gabapentin, Plan B for contraceptive backup, and recommendations for genetic testing to confirm beta thalassemia. Follow-up with her primary care provider was advised.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period

___ with history of tracheobronchomalacia s/p tracheostomy,

ACTIVE ISSUES:
===================
# Tracheitis: Patient presented with symptoms similar to prior 
admissions, with complaints of purulent sputum but no clear 
infectious symptoms, as she was afebrile without lekocytosis and 
had a clear admission chest film. The patient had four recent 
admissions with similar presentations during which no infection 
was found. She had several contaminated sputum cultures, but a 
tracheal aspirate obtained by IP grew S. Aureus and H. Flu. The 
patient was started on a course of vancomycin 1g IV Q12H for 10 
days ___ the hospital to be continued as an outpatient (start 
___, end ___. During the hospitalization, the 
patient was continued on her home tracheostomy care (Portex 
Thermovent® T2 heat and moisture exchanger (HME) during the day, 
use a trach mask w/humidified oxygen, clindamycin to 
tracheostomy site BID) as well as symptom control including 
guaifenisin, DuoNebs, and Claritin. The patient has close 
follow-up scheduled with both ORL and her PCP.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
===================
# Odynophagia, dysphagia: Prior to presentation the patient 
experienced 3 days of odynophagia associated with solids and 
liquids. She also reports sensation of food feeling stuck; 
however she cannot localize this. She has a h/o Schatzki's ring 
visualized on EGD (___), a normal barium swallow (___), and CT 
neck (___) without esophageal findings. The symptoms were 
monitored with option to repeat a video swallow study if 
symptoms persisted. Over course of stay the patient improved and 
was discharged with antibiotiocs after a tracheal culture was 
positive for S. Aureus.

# Chronic pain: Patient on narcotics contract with PCP. Has 
requested additional doses of pain medications on previous 
discharges due to ""increased use at home"". Home pain regimen 
containing acetaminophen, fluoxetine, gabapentin, lidocaine 
patch, and oxycodone was continued during the hospitalization, 
and Dilaudid was added for breakthrough pain. The patient was 
placed on an aggressive bowel regimen while inpatient to prevent 
constipation. The patient was discharged on her home pain 
regimen with instruction to follow up with PCP for additional 
prescriptions or changes.

# Acute on chronic microcytic anemia: Patient with history of 
iron deficiency, recent work-up notable for hemoglobinopathy 
(beta thal w/high F vs delta-beta thalassemia). No signs of 
active bleeding during this admission and the patient was 
continued on ferrous sulfate.
  
#GERD: Stable during the admission; home omeprazole and 
ranitidine was continued.
